content: Stearic acid, also known by its IUPAC systematic name octadecanoic acid, is a type of saturated fatty acid commonly found in both animal and vegetable fats and oils. It is a waxy solid with the chemical formula CH3(CH2)16COOH. The name stearic is derived from the Greek word stéar, meaning tallow. The term stearate refers to the salts and esters of stearic acid. Stearic acid is produced by hydrolyzing triglycerides in animal fat using water under high pressure and temperature. It can also be synthesized through the hydrogenation of certain unsaturated vegetable oils. Commercially available stearic acid is often a mixture of stearic acid and palmitic acid, although purified stearic acid can be obtained separately. Stearic acid has a wide range of applications. It is used as an ingredient in the production of candles, soaps, plastics, oil pastels, cosmetics, and as a softening agent for rubber. In soap manufacturing, it is particularly useful for hardening soaps made from vegetable oils. Additionally, stearic acid serves as a parting compound in plaster casting processes, where a solution of powdered stearic acid dissolved in water is applied to surfaces to facilitate separation after casting. Esters of stearic acid, such as glycol stearate and glycol distearate, are employed in cosmetic products like shampoos and soaps to create a pearlescent effect. These esters are added in molten form and allowed to crystallize under controlled conditions. In the field of pyrotechnics, stearic acid is used to coat metal powders, such as aluminum and iron, to prevent oxidation and extend the storage life of compositions. It is also used as a hardener in candies, often in combination with simple sugars or corn syrup. Stearic acid undergoes typical reactions of saturated carboxylic acids, including reduction to stearyl alcohol and esterification with various alcohols. Compared to palmitic acid, stearic acid is less likely to be converted into cholesterol esters and is less readily incorporated into such esters. These findings suggest that stearic acid may have a lower health risk compared to other saturated fatty acids.
